topics.title: The interview as a genre and its divided reputation

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the interview has become a commonplace of journalism and why opinions about it vary.
Compare the admiring and hostile views of the interview presented by Silvester.
Explain Denis Brian's view of the interview as a powerful medium of communication.
Identify the attitudes of Naipaul, Carroll and Kipling towards interviews.
Analyse the gap between what Kipling and Wells said about interviews and what they did.
Interpret Saul Bellow's image of interviews as thumbprints on his windpipe.

topics.title: Umberto Eco: one purpose and the use of interstices

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Eco's varied work is unified by the same ethical and philosophical interests.
Interpret what Eco means by working in the interstices of life.

topics.title: Eco's narrative scholarship and his identity as an academic

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how Eco's dissertation led him to write scholarly work as the story of research.
Recall when and how Eco began writing novels, in contrast with Roland Barthes.
Evaluate Eco's view of himself as a professor who writes novels on Sundays.

topics.title: The Name of the Rose and the mystery of its success

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Eco was not puzzled that a serious novel found a mass audience.
Analyse Eco's argument that the success of a book cannot be predicted.

topics.title: Discourse linkers, signallers and reporting an interview
topics.ncert_sections: Noticing discourse linkers and signallers; Writing

concepts.learning_objective: Identify how reference pronouns and repetition link the turns of a conversation.
Recognise phrases that signal a shift of topic in a conversation.
Transfer the salient points of an interview into a concise report.
